To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the TCR-mediated selection of autoreactive T cells is accompanied by the coordinated expression of a number of genes that are involved in apoptosis, DNA recombinaion, antigen processing and cell adhesion.

TCR engagement in vivo induces a gene expression profile that is distinct from that of non-activated DP thymocytes, that the expression of this profile is regulated in a developmental stage-specific manner and that the profile involves genes that regulate apoptosis, DNA recombina-tion, antigen processing and thymocyte adhesion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel genes involved in thymocyte selection.
the identification of genes that are involved in the TCR-mediated selection of thymocytes and that can serve as markers for the study of T-cell development and selection in vivo.
the identification of genes that are differentially regulated in DP thymocytes during TCR-mediated negative selection in vivo and with the identification of the molecular mechanisms involved.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TCR-activated apoptosis pathway involves a large number of genes that are coordinately engaged in the biological processes that lead to the elimination of autoreactive thrymocytes.
TCR-induced gene expression in thymi is a complex process, involving a wide variety of genes, and that the selection of TCRs occurs through multiple mechanisms.

TCR-mediated thymocyte selection is an integrated process involving multiple pathways and that the expression profiles of genes engaged in this process vary according to the stage of development of the thymocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
thymic selection is a dynamic process involving a complex interplay between multiple genes.
TCR engagement of DP thymocytes induces the expression of a large array of genes involved in the biological process of apoptosis.
the TCR-induced gene expression profile is highly regulated in the thymus and that this regulation is dependent on the developmental stage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TCR-mediated thymocyte selection is a highly coordinated process involving the engagement of many different genes, including those involved in apoptosis, cell adhesion and signal transduction.
TCR-induced gene expression in thymeocytes in vivo is a dynamic and complex process.
TCR signaling in vivo leads to the activation of a large number of genes that participate in the apoptotic process.
